messages:
sanjay: quick RFC follow-up — we need to pick a canonical layout for MHA kernels. i'm leaning NHWC for better per-head contiguous reads, but worried about the extra transpose in some prep paths. thoughts?

maria: NHWC makes the per-head matmul vectorization simpler, yes. contiguous QKV (Q,K,V interleaved per-head) reduces strided gathers. downside: more work when exporting from frameworks that default to NCHW.

kjohnson: Can we keep both in runtime and pick per-model? that adds complexity to kernel selection logic but avoids forcing transposes at model load.

alexa_research: +1 for per-model selection. concrete perf from my microbench: NHWC contiguous QKV wins ~8-12% on sequence length 512 for bsz1 on A100 when we fuse softmax and dropout. NCHW wins for huge batch sizes due to better batch-major GEMM paths.

bench-bot: bench results (short):
```
model: mha-small
hw: a100
bsz=1 seqlen=512 heads=16 d_head=64
NHWC_contig_qkv: 28.1 ms
NCHW_interleaved: 30.6 ms
transpose cost (NCHW->NHWC): 1.9 ms
```

sanjay: good data. question: should we assume kernel authors will accept stride arguments and implement both memory access patterns in one kernel, or produce two specialized kernels (nhwc vs nchw) and let selector choose?

maria: unifying via stride params is elegant but often hurts perf because the compiler can't optimize for unknown stride. two specialized kernels + small selector gives best peak perf. selector complexity is mostly config table.

kjohnson: also consider cache aliasing: interleaved QKV with stride puts K/V pointers on different cache lines per head; that can kill prefetch. contiguous per-head eliminates that. microbench showed 10-15% fewer L2 misses.

alexa_research: interface boundary idea: KernelDescriptor { layout: "NHWC"|"NCHW", qkv_packing: "contiguous"|"interleaved", head_stride, seq_stride, fused_ops: ["softmax","dropout"] }
runtime-oncall: +1 to explicit descriptor. makes tracing/debugging easier. put selection hooks in the model->runtime binder.

sanjay: implementation plan proposal:
1) add two kernels for MHA (nhwc_contig_qkv, nchw_interleaved) with identical signatures except they assume different memory layout semantics.
2) introduce a light-weight KernelSelector that picks based on: hw, batch, seqlen, head_dim, packing, and whether softmax/dropout are fused.
3) if model loader sees a mismatch, do export-time transpose and mark cost in the model metadata.

maria: small nit — don't always transpose at load. allow lazy transpose and cache transposed buffers per model @ runtime to avoid upfront cost for rarely used models.

kjohnson: about fused ops: some kernels will prefer NHWC because they can do contiguous reductions. we should record a "fusion_preference" score per kernel during onboarding so selector can compare expected end-to-end latency, not just raw matmul perf.

bench-bot: added fusion_preference to kernel catalog entry for nhwc_contig_qkv = 0.9, nchw_interleaved = 0.6

alexa_research: also consider alignment/padding: heads*head_dim should be padded to 64B or 128B to help vector loads. runtime should provide a align_up utility and kernel descriptors should expose required alignment so loader can pad tensors.

runtime-oncall: ops for rollout: (a) add descriptors + catalog metadata, (b) implement two kernels, (c) kernel selector + heuristics, (d) lazy transpose + cache, (e) onboarding doc for kernel devs with alignment/fusion guidelines.

sanjay: ok going to sketch RFC for these steps. quick vote: are we OK with specialized kernels + selector (vs stride-param unified kernel)? react with :+1: or :-1:.

maria: :+1:
kjohnson: :+1:
alexa_research: :+1:
runtime-oncall: :+1:
sanjay: thanks — i'll draft the RFC and include bench artifacts and the selector pseudocode. examples to include:
```
// selector pseudocode
if hw == "a100" and bsz == 1 and seqlen <= 1024 and fusion == true:
  pick nhwc_contig_qkv
elif bsz > 8:
  pick nchw_interleaved
else
  pick kernel with higher fusion_preference
```

sanjay: tagging infra for kernel rollout planning @kjohnson @runtime-oncall.

kjohnson: will add cost accounting hooks so the console can show when a transpose was applied at load time and how much it added.

alexa_research: nice. please include a short 'how to bench' doc for reproducibility (seed, config, warmup iterations).

sanjay: will do. end.
